# Database schema

PostgreSQL, managed with Prisma. The schema lives in `backend/prisma/schema/*.prisma`
(one file per domain). SQL migrations are in `backend/prisma/migrations`.

## Conventions

* Tables are `snake_case` plurals, columns `snake_case`.
* Primary keys are UUID v7, generated by the application, so they sort by creation time
  and need no particular PostgreSQL version.
* Timestamps are `timestamptz(3)`.
* **Money is `NUMERIC(18,2)` (rupees). There is no floating-point money anywhere.**
* Enums are real PostgreSQL enum types.
* Soft deletion (`deleted_at`) only where history matters (users, posts, reels, stories,
  comments, media). Financial and audit tables are never deleted.

## Migrations

| Migration | Contents |
|---|---|
| `20261009000000_extensions` | `pg_trgm`, `pgcrypto` (both "trusted", so the DB owner can create them) |
| `20261009000010_init` | Tables, enums, ordinary indexes, foreign keys. Generated: `prisma migrate diff --from-empty --to-schema prisma/schema --script` |
| `20261009000100_integrity` | Hand-written: CHECK constraints, partial and trigram indexes, append-only triggers, the ledger triggers |
| `20261009000200_admin_invites` | Staff invitation fields (temporary password expiry, forced change) |
| `20261009000300_media_job_scheduling` | Media jobs can be delayed and carry parameters; adds the `COMPOSE` job type used to assemble reels |
| `20261009000400_music_drafts` | A track may be a draft with no audio yet (`duration_ms >= 0`), but a live track must have audio, a preview and a length (`music_tracks_active_complete`) |
| `20261009000500_reach_stage7_columns` | A Reach configuration can be created by the system (no staff creator); reward cycles keep a summary of what closing them did |

Apply with `npm run db:migrate` (`prisma migrate deploy`). `migrate dev` is not used: it
refuses to run non-interactively, and generating SQL by `migrate diff` lets hand-written
rules live in the same history. `npm run db:verify` applies every migration to a throw-away
PostgreSQL and prints what it built.

Before the first real environment the initial migration may be regenerated. After that,
every change is a new migration folder (`npm run db:migrate:create -- <name>`), reviewed
like code, and never edited once applied.

## Integrity enforced by the database

These hold regardless of which code, script or person writes the data, and each is proven
by a test in `backend/tests/db` run against a real PostgreSQL.

| Rule | How |
|---|---|
| A journal's debits equal its credits | deferred constraint trigger on `financial_ledger_entries` |
| A ledger balance changes only through an entry | `BEFORE INSERT` trigger applies the entry to the account under a row lock; a guard trigger refuses any other change |
| A creator's balance can never be negative | `CHECK` on `ledger_accounts` (so concurrent withdrawals cannot overdraw: tested with 25 at once against a balance that covers 10) |
| Ledger entries, journals and the audit log are append-only | `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` and `BEFORE TRUNCATE` triggers |
| The same journal cannot post twice | unique `idempotency_key` |
| Aadhaar numbers are never stored, not even encrypted or hashed | `CHECK` on `kyc_documents` |
| An engagement row (like, save, share, comment, reach event or score) points at exactly one target | `CHECK num_nonnulls(...) = 1` |
| One live identity case per user; one primary bank account per user; no duplicate account | partial unique indexes |
| Exactly one active Reach configuration; an active one cannot be edited | partial unique index and a guard trigger |
| An active music track names its territories and has its audio, preview and length; a restricted track is never active | `CHECK` |
| Usernames are lower-case `[a-z0-9._]{3,30}`, e-mail is lower-case, phone is E.164 | `CHECK` |
| A user has an e-mail or a phone | `CHECK` |
| Ad spend never exceeds budget | `CHECK` |

## Sensitive data and retention

| Class | Fields | Protection | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Credentials | `users.password_hash`, `admin_users.password_hash` | argon2id hash | life of the account |
| Session secrets | `user_sessions.refresh_token_hash`, `admin_sessions.*` | SHA-256 of a random token; the token itself is never stored | until expiry, then purged |
| One-time codes | `otp_challenges.code_hash` | HMAC, short expiry, attempt limit | purged shortly after expiry |
| 2FA secrets | `*.two_factor_secret_enc` | AES-256-GCM (field encryption) | until 2FA is turned off |
| Identity data | `kyc_profiles.*_enc`, `kyc_documents.number_enc` | AES-256-GCM; a keyed HMAC "blind index" detects duplicates without decrypting | `retention_until`, then deleted by a worker (to be set with legal counsel) |
| Identity documents (files) | `media_assets` with purpose `KYC_DOCUMENT` | private bucket, never a public URL, signed access logged | same as above |
| Aadhaar | last four digits only | never stored in any other form | n/a |
| Bank accounts | `payout_accounts.*_enc`, `account_number_index` | AES-256-GCM plus blind index; shown as last four digits | while the account is in use, then per policy |
| Tax identity | `tax_profiles.pan_enc` | AES-256-GCM plus blind index | per tax-record requirements |
| Contact details | `users.email`, `users.phone` | masked for staff without `users.read_contact` | until deletion |
| Audit trail | `audit_logs` | append-only | long-term; access to protected data is flagged `sensitive` |
| Money | `financial_ledger_entries` | append-only, double entry | permanent (legal record) |

The keys for field encryption come from the environment (a secrets manager in
production), carry a key id so they can be rotated, and are never in the repository. See
[`security.md`](security.md).

Retention periods are placeholders in configuration. They are legal decisions, not
engineering ones, and need review by qualified Indian counsel before launch (DPDP Act,
RBI payment rules, tax record-keeping).

## Scale notes

* `reach_events` is the highest-volume table. Before launch it should be range-partitioned by
  month, with old partitions rolled into daily aggregates. The `dedupe_key` unique index must
  then include the partition key.
* `notifications`, `security_events`, `audit_logs` and `financial_ledger_entries` grow
  without bound and are indexed for recent-first reads; archive by partition when needed.
* Feed queries read through partial indexes that match exactly the predicate they use
  (public, approved, not deleted), keyed by `(published_at DESC, id DESC)` for cursor
  pagination.
* Counters (`likes_count`, `followers_count`, ...) are denormalised and updated in the same
  transaction as the row they count; a reconciliation job recomputes them.
